title: Flatten exceptions, notes, subordinate lists, and definitions into paragraphs
description: Flattening preserves words but destroys ownership, ordering, scope, and the distinction between normative and explanatory material.
author: bcast

title: Represent definitions, lists, notes, tables, footnotes, and unsupported regions explicitly
description: Shared structural node types and code-family metadata preserve source organization while exceptions and semantic clause roles remain in later family-specific stages where evidence supports them.
author: bcast

title: Preserve references as evidence-backed relationships rather than copied text
description: References retain source spans and target locators or target domains; unresolved references remain unresolved rather than being forced into the current document.
author: bcast

title: Selected NEC clauses gained reviewable semantic projections
description: Article 100 definitions and Sections 90.5, 110.2, 110.3, 110.14, 110.16, and 110.26 preserve clauses, exceptions, notes, references, tags, and exact spans without claiming compliance interpretation.
author: bcast

title: Distinguish actual NEC edition changes from extraction errors
description: A parser difference between 2017 and 2020 could reflect amended text, layout drift, missing content, or a parser defect; the evidence streams must remain independent.
author: bcast

title: Treat secondary change summaries as authoritative edition deltas
description: Summaries can identify candidates but omit rejected proposals, procedural reversals, errata, and exact issued text.
author: bcast

title: Use NFPA development records to build an expected-change oracle
description: Public inputs, comments, actions, TIAs, errata, and Council outcomes can predict where change should appear, but only as process evidence.
author: bcast

title: Treat independently observed issued editions as controlling text evidence
description: Expected changes cannot fabricate observed 2020 text. The 2017 and 2020 parsers must run independently before reconciliation.
author: bcast

title: Authorized 2020 NEC source was not available for reconciliation
description: The expected-change machinery could be exercised, but observed-change reconciliation remained blocked without a lawful source artifact.
author: bcast

title: NEC 2020 expected changelog remains branch-bound and non-authoritative
description: The branch models process evidence and diagnostics, but main does not claim a 2020 parser, a complete changelog, or observed edition reconciliation.
author: bcast

title: Adapt the compiler to the supplied 2018 IBC PDF
description: IBC provided a second major code family to test whether the NEC machinery reflected shared document concepts or NEC-specific accidents.
author: bcast

title: Import the prior private PDF parser as a runtime dependency
description: That would couple public operation to private code, obscure provenance, and make the repository unreproducible for other users.
author: bcast

title: Adapt useful parser architecture without taking a private dependency
description: Geometry, reading-order, source-map, and validation ideas were reimplemented in repository-owned code with synthetic public tests and private source execution.
author: bcast

title: IBC exposed glyph-oriented text, spacing defects, mixed columns, tables, scripts, and publisher furniture
description: The source required visual-baseline grouping, word-boundary repair, hyphenation evidence, page-local reading modes, and table exclusion before structural parsing.
author: bcast

title: Limit the initial IBC production slice to Chapters 1 through 3
description: The branch exercised opening matter, administrative provisions, hundreds of definitions, and ruled tables while failing closed for unsupported chapters.
author: bcast

title: Design an IBC-specific hierarchy builder over neutral primitives
description: Decimal section parents, Parts, enumerations, exceptions, definitions, tables, figures, notes, and appendix-prefixed locators require ICC conventions rather than NEC marker rules.
author: bcast

title: IBC findings changed the architecture without becoming current main support
description: The layout branch has substantial private-source validation, but the ingestion and hierarchy stack remains unmerged; complete-edition and appendix support are not claimed.
author: bcast

title: Share parser machinery without pretending all code families use one grammar
description: NEC, ICC, and NFPA publications share provenance and tree concepts but differ materially in numbering, editorial conventions, annexes, tables, and layout.
author: bcast

title: Use one grammar for NEC, IBC, and NFPA documents
description: Universal marker and numbering assumptions would misclassify lists, parts, decimal sections, annex correspondences, and edition-specific layout.
author: bcast

title: Share source identity, spans, diagnostics, tables, and generic node contracts
description: Publication-neutral primitives provide interoperability and validation without deciding how a source family recognizes those structures.
author: bcast

title: Keep NEC, IBC, ICC evidence, and NFPA grammars separately versioned
description: Each family can evolve its parser and evidence rules without destabilizing the neutral AST or claiming support for unrelated editions.
author: bcast

title: Permit edition-specific profiles when evidence shows layout or editorial change
description: A source-family parser may select an edition profile or fail closed; premature normalization is less trustworthy than explicit compatibility limits.
author: bcast

title: The architecture became neutral at contracts and specific at grammars
description: Shared layout/evidence utilities feed source-family adapters and hierarchy builders; current support claims are expressed per source family, edition, and validated region.
author: bcast

title: Investigate and parse the 2019 NFPA 13 clause hierarchy
description: NFPA 13 tested chapters, nested numbered clauses, annex explanations, external-standard references, revision markers, and table geometry beyond the NEC slice.
author: bcast

title: NFPA 13 source access and generated text had to remain local
description: The branch could publish source-safe code, schemas, reviewed non-reconstructive cases, and aggregate receipts but not the PDF or full text-bearing bundle.
author: bcast

title: Use a provenance-pinned local extractor and strict bundle contract
description: The branch records producer commit, engine and wrapper identity, environment, source ownership, spans, relationships, diagnostics, and deterministic output.
author: bcast

title: Synthesized Annex A ancestry containers are structural, not explanatory relationships
description: Only explicit Annex A correspondence nodes can emit an explains relationship; parent containers must not manufacture semantic links.
author: bcast

title: Distinguish internal, external-standard, and unspecified-document targets
description: NFPA, ASTM, ASME, AWWA, ANSI, UL, IEEE, and ISO citations cannot all be treated as locators in NFPA 13; unresolved ownership remains explicit.
author: bcast

title: Table geometry can be conservative while figure and diagram semantics remain unsupported
description: The branch preserves table subtrees and diagnostics but does not infer semantic spans, units, figure meaning, or engineering interpretation from layout alone.
author: bcast

title: NFPA 13 demonstrated broader scalability but remains unmerged
description: Complete-source deterministic validation on the draft is strong evidence for the branch, not evidence that main currently supports NFPA 13 or every construct.
author: bcast

title: Determine how UL White Book and related technical sources should connect to code structure
description: Listings, categories, certification files, marking guidance, and product observations are not prescriptive model-code clauses even when code provisions reference them.
author: bcast

title: UL source records model categories, certifications, products, holders, and dated observations
description: These entities need temporal and evidentiary relationships that do not fit a chapter-section-clause tree.
author: bcast

title: Put UL categories and certifications directly into the building-code document AST
description: This would collapse prescriptive code structure, reference material, certification state, and equipment lineage into one misleading tree.
author: bcast

title: Keep UL White Book compilation and certification lineage in Electrical Equipment Lineage
description: That repository owns the source-specific compiler, CCN index, Product iQ snapshots, equipment relationships, and publication boundary.
author: bcast
